_comment: ei-json baseline digest for the axibridge byte-identity guard (M17 Task 2). See ei-byte-identity.test.mjs for the regeneration procedure. Regenerated 2026-08-27. The baseline had gone STALE for the SECOND time -- it was last captured during MPVE, which landed in v1.5.0, and six releases (v1.5.0 -> v1.7.1) moved the document without anyone recapturing it. It stayed hidden because main's Linux job dies earlier, at the version-sync gate, and never reaches the Node SDK tests at all. Anchor verified rather than assumed: a v1.5.0 (7a4e8fa) build reproduces the OLD recorded digest exactly (3658140 / 4c53bf51...), which is what pins the drift window. The drift is +9,350 chars, attributed by top-level key: players +7,940, buffMap +808, personalDamageMods +369 (new in v1.7.1) and skillMap +211. The players growth is entirely inside `support` and adds NO new player-level keys -- it is the v1.6.x arcdps-parity cleanse buckets (condiCleanseArcdps, boonStripsArcdps*, condiCleanseMinions, ...). Crucially for axibridge, nothing it already consumes changed: every leaf value of the old document was compared against the new one -- 373,534 values, of which 52 moved, and all 52 are skillMap.sNNN.name going "Skill NNN" -> a real name (s1066 -> Resurrect, s30498 -> Resolve, s12854 -> Ice Whirl Combo, ...), which is the v1.6.2 SkillIDs.cs symbol rung. Zero values regressed and zero keys went missing. Determinism was confirmed per this test's own mandate: two consecutive captures at the recorded sourceCommit agree on both length and sha256. sourceCommit is now a full sha, not a branch name -- the previous entry ("mpve-pve-encounter-identification") was a branch that had been deleted after merge, so the anchor it named was unresolvable when this drift was finally investigated. || Regenerated 2026-09-01 (THIRD staleness). Drift window 14ab2f68 -> 1db5808, +736 code units (3667490 -> 3668226). Attributed by leaf-diff of a worktree build at the recorded anchor against HEAD: EXACTLY 4 keys ADDED, 0 removed, 0 changed -- skillMap.s23294 'Generic Knockdown', s23295 'Generic Knockback and Pull', s23296 'Generic Float', s23299 'Generic Control Effect From Buff'. These are the arcdps generic control effect ids that v1.10.0's CC attribution lane started naming; purely additive, and nothing axibridge already consumes moved. The anchor was VERIFIED not assumed: a build at 14ab2f68 reproduces the previous recorded pair (3667490 / 0310eaa9...) exactly. The blocks.focus merge (47ca3c4) is NOT implicated -- a build at its first parent 1db5808 produces the same 3668226 / 1a91803b... as HEAD, byte for byte. Same hiding mechanism as last time: main's Linux job died at the version-sync gate for every release from v1.8.0 to v1.10.2 and never reached the Node SDK tests, so four releases' worth of CI never ran this guard. Determinism reconfirmed: two consecutive captures agree on length and sha256. || Re-anchored 2026-09-02 to ad96077c3d649a1eb7a1cd91559a8b1dc9339bd9 (HEAD of main). NOT a drift entry: this is a fresh capture that reproduced the recorded pair exactly (3668226 / 1a91803b...), so jsonStringLength and sha256 are unchanged and only sourceCommit moved forward from 47ca3c4. Motivation: the previous anchor was captured by hand on 2026-09-01 and had never been confirmed by CI, because main's Linux job died at the version-sync gate before reaching the Node SDK tests. ci.yml commit ad96077 split that gate into a standalone job, and run 33595641388 became the first CI run to actually execute this guard since v1.7.1 -- it logged the identical length and digest. Re-anchoring records that the digest is now verified at a commit whose CI ran it, rather than at an unverified one. Determinism reconfirmed per this test's mandate: two consecutive captures from a release build at ad96077 agree on both length and sha256. || Regenerated 2026-09-04 for an INTENTIONAL additive change (not drift): dist_rows_ei_json now emits `playerTotal` on `totalDamageTaken` rows, carrying SkillRow::player_total -- the arcdps-style player-sourced refinement -- through to the EI shape so axibridge can offer the incoming-damage filter without reading the native container. Drift window 30fc8fc -> HEAD, +24,285 code units (3668226 -> 3692511). The anchor was VERIFIED not assumed: a worktree build at the PREVIOUS recorded sourceCommit lineage reproduces the previous pair (3668226 / 1a91803b...) exactly at 30fc8fc, so ad96077 -> 30fc8fc contributed ZERO drift and the whole delta is this change. Attributed by leaf-diff of the two builds: 1,391 leaves ADDED, 0 removed, 0 changed; every added leaf is named `playerTotal` and every one sits under `players[].totalDamageTaken`. Outgoing and per-target rows are untouched because the emit is gated on the field own Option, which is None there. On this fixture coverage is 100% (1,391 of 1,391 taken rows carry the key) and the refinement invariant holds on every row (playerTotal <= totalDamage, 0 violations); the fixture is ~100.00% player-sourced (1,056,771 of 1,056,781), so it exercises SHAPE but not the split -- real WvW logs with siege and guards are where the two numbers diverge. Determinism reconfirmed per this test mandate: two consecutive captures agree on both length and sha256, on both sides of the diff.
